name: Hoang Nguyen
description: Hoang Nguyen leads an independent research group working across data science, deep learning, bioinformatics, health informatics and computer-aided drug design.
intro: I work at the intersection of data science, artificial intelligence and the life sciences. My research connects computational methods with questions in biology, healthcare and drug discovery.
about: My name is Hoang Nguyen. I am a lecturer and researcher based in Wellington, New Zealand. My work focuses on applying machine learning, deep learning, and artificial intelligence to the life, molecular, and health sciences.

I lead the Hoang Nguyen Research Group, where I serve as principal supervisor and project coordinator. The group brings together researchers and research assistants to address shared computational questions and turn methods and tools into research outcomes.

research.name: Data Science
research.description: Predictive modelling, data curation and evaluation methods for applied research. We are interested in how data quality, study design and validation affect the conclusions a model can support.
research.collaboration: Research datasets, reproducible analysis and the evaluation of predictive models.

research.name: Deep Learning
research.description: Graph neural networks, transformers, multimodal learning and generative models. We study representations and learning strategies for complex scientific data.
research.collaboration: Representation learning, complementary data sources and comparisons with strong baselines.

research.name: Bioinformatics
research.description: Computational analysis of biological sequences and molecular data, including peptide prediction and the identification of functional sequence features.
research.collaboration: Biological datasets, sequence-based prediction and computational questions supported by experimental context.

research.name: Health Informatics
research.description: Data science and AI applied to health information and clinical questions. Our interests include medical prediction, human–computer interaction and the careful evaluation of technologies for healthcare.
research.collaboration: Clinically grounded questions, external validation and evidence synthesis.

research.name: Computer-aided Drug Design
research.description: Molecular property prediction, drug–target modelling and computational approaches to molecular design. Our published work also includes molecular data resources and curation software.
research.collaboration: Molecular datasets, computational screening and modelling linked to experimental follow-up.
